spec_match.rationale: Private Verification Tokens have no web-facing API on this build, so the pages exercise Private State Tokens — the shipping mechanism the proposal builds on — and the index says so in its own section rather than blurring the two. Every call is real: both document methods against five issuers, and the request option's grammar swept across fourteen values.

interactive.rationale: A live issuer prober with a free-text field; an option builder that constructs a real Request on every change plus a sweep of every value; and a timed challenge the reader actually solves, compared against a timed token check.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index leads on who bears the cost of anti-fraud friction, which is the proposal's own framing, and states plainly that the newer proposal is not what is being measured.

edge_cases.rationale: Insecure and malformed issuers rejected; an issuer URL carrying a path accepted silently; an unknown operation and an out-of-range version rejected at conversion; a wrong answer to the challenge, which is where the real cost of a puzzle is.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/6210457816924160 on the index and all three concept pages, with the Trust Token specification, Chrome's Private State Tokens documentation and RFC 9578.

conformance.rationale: Six immutable assertions: both query methods exist; a valid issuer answers with a boolean; an http issuer is refused; the request option is read; an unknown operation is rejected; and a known one is accepted, as the control that makes the rejection meaningful.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150: 3/3, 24 assertions. Verified: three of five issuers accepted and answering false, two rejected with TypeError; all three surface members present including the fetch option probed with a getter; six of fourteen swept option values accepted with the rest naming their offending value; and the challenge timed at 0.4s against a 0.4ms token check. NOT verified: any issuance or redemption. There is no issuer to talk to, and the pages say so rather than firing a request at a made-up origin and reporting the network error as if it meant something.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the issuer results, the swept accept counts, and both measured durations.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px minimums including the challenge tiles, and every wide table in its own scroll container.

accessibility.rationale: The challenge tiles are real buttons in a labelled group with aria-pressed and per-tile accessible names, so the puzzle is operable from the keyboard and legible to a screen reader — which is more than the thing it is imitating usually manages, and is the point the page is making. Results are announced through aria-live.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Control grids auto-fit; the tile grid is a four-column grid capped at 22rem so it stays thumb-sized on a phone; every table scrolls in its own container.

openQuestions.title: No issuance or redemption has been exercised
openQuestions.detail: The whole mechanism is a round trip between a browser and an issuer, and none of it happens here — the pages measure the two query methods and the request grammar, which is everything reachable without an issuer. Standing up a real issuer endpoint that speaks the Privacy Pass protocol would let a fourth concept show a token being issued and spent, and is a substantial piece of server work rather than a page.

openQuestions.title: The visitor table is an argument, not a measurement
openQuestions.detail: The who-pays table on the friction page is the proposal's reasoning written out, and is labelled as such twice. It is the most persuasive thing on the feature and the least evidenced, which is an uncomfortable combination — worth revisiting if published data on challenge rates by visitor class becomes citable.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible selection grid with pressed state
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use real buttons with aria-pressed for a toggle grid, give each one an accessible name, and group them under a label.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The challenge tiles are buttons with aria-pressed and per-tile labels inside a role=group labelled by the prompt, so the puzzle is keyboard-operable and readable — deliberately, since the page's argument is about who challenges exclude.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive solves the puzzle by clicking the correct tiles and asserts the correct-answer message.

guidanceConsulted.query: controls that build an API call and validate as you type
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Recompute on input, show the resulting value, and report validation failures next to the control that caused them.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The option builder reconstructs a real Request on every change and shows both the call and the browser's verdict; the sweep table names the option, the value and the message together.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive changes the operation to an invalid value and asserts the TypeError appears in the verdict.

summary: Three concepts about a proposal with no API yet, built on the shipping mechanism underneath it. Two claims were corrected by measurement: an issuer URL with a path is accepted rather than rejected (so that mistake fails silently), and the rejection messages are considerably better than the page first said — they walk the property chain and name the offending value.
